etymologies.etymologyHTML: From formula +‎ -ate.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To put into a clear and definite form of statement or expression.

quote.citation: 1876, George Perkins Marsh, Mediaeval and Modern Saints and Miracles:
quote.text: The Assembly then formulated its demands, which were thirty in number, including the removal of all Huguenot temples built near churches

quote.citation: 1988, Andrew Radford, Transformational Grammar, Cambridge: University Press, →ISBN, page 19:
quote.text: Another source of evidence supporting the conclusion that children learn language by formulating a set of rules comes from the errors that they produce. A case in point are overgeneralized past tense forms like comed, goed, seed, buyed, bringed, etc. frequently used by young children.
